# Spawnflow

> Laravel package that collapses the API request lifecycle into one fluent chain and serves your data WITH its form attached: field types, validation rules, and who-can-touch-what, resolved per role and record state. One declaration per resource; TypeScript + Zod clients generated from the same contract the live endpoint serves.

Key facts for code generation:

- The chain: `(new Flow)->spawn($request)->auth()->resolve('posts')->ask('POST', $id)->fields()->validate()->save($request->all())->present()`
- One resource = one FieldSet (field descriptors) + one FieldContext enum (role × record-state permissions). Scaffold both from a real table: `php artisan spawnflow:resource Post --generate` — the generated FieldSet self-registers via `#[SpawnSubject]`.
- Two orthogonal permission axes: the context enum answers WHO may touch a field in WHAT record state (server-resolved variants); eligibility rules answer "given the form's current VALUES, is this field visible/enabled" (`->visibleWhen(...)/enabledWhen(...)` with restricted JSON Logic conditions, evaluated identically in PHP and JS, fail-closed). Never put role checks in rules.
- Groups (`FieldSet::groups()`, `Group::make('billing', [...])->visibleWhen(...)`) are rule-bearing sections; hidden group hides members (AND composition).
- The schema contract (docs/schema-contract.md) is the single source of truth: `GET /spawnflow/schema/{subject}/{id?}` serves it; `php artisan spawnflow:generate` emits TypeScript types + Zod schemas from the same serializer — no drift possible.
- Write path enforces everything: variant-ineligible and rule-ineligible fields are discarded on save, never trusted from the client.
- Livewire renderer: `<livewire:spawnflow-form subject="posts" :record-id="$id" />` — ONE generic schema-interpreting component, auto-registered when Livewire is installed; eligibility re-evaluates server-side per update; saves flow through the same Flow chain as HTTP.
- SSE invalidation (opt-in, `spawnflow.events`): `GET /spawnflow/events` streams `change` signals on Flow writes — signals only, clients refetch via existing endpoints; `subscribeToChanges()` in @spawnflow/core.

## MCP

- Optional MCP server (requires laravel/mcp; config spawnflow.mcp.enabled): tools list-subjects, get-schema, check-eligibility, validate-payload (dry-run, never writes), scaffold-resource + generate-types (local stdio only), and runtime CRUD (create/update/delete/get/list/field-options) that runs the full Flow chain and returns the PERSISTED record. Resources serve this file, the schema contract doc, and the conformance fixtures. See docs/mcp.md.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): install, chain API, context enums, escape hatches
- [Schema contract](docs/schema-contract.md): the wire format — descriptors, structured rules, eligibility envelopes, resolved verdicts, groups
- [MCP server](docs/mcp.md): tools, transports, security model
- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): feature history

## Frontend

- `@spawnflow/core` (js/core): contract types, cross-runtime eligibility evaluator, rule→Zod compiler, HTTP client — framework-agnostic
- `@spawnflow/react-shadcn` (js/react-shadcn): `<SpawnForm>` renderer; also distributed as a shadcn registry item (`npx shadcn add <registry-url>/r/spawn-form.json`) so the presentational source lives in YOUR repo, editable
- Conformance: resources/conformance/eligibility-fixtures.json pins PHP↔JS evaluator parity — change semantics there first, never in one runtime
